claims.text: Existing high-entropy alloys have limited magnetocaloric properties.
Doping high-entropy alloys with oxygen can improve their magnetocaloric properties.
Doping high-entropy alloys with nitrogen can improve their magnetocaloric properties.
The proposed doping intervention is to add oxygen or nitrogen to high-entropy alloys.
The proposed effect is expected near room temperature and across various magnetic fields.
Adding oxygen or nitrogen can change the microstructure of high-entropy alloys.
Adding oxygen or nitrogen can change the phase composition of high-entropy alloys.
Changes in microstructure and phase composition caused by oxygen or nitrogen doping result in improved magnetocaloric properties.
Oxygen or nitrogen doping is predicted to increase magnetic entropy change.
Oxygen or nitrogen doping is predicted to increase refrigerant capacity.
Current processing techniques and alloy designs limit the proposed improvement strategy.
The exact mechanisms by which oxygen or nitrogen doping would improve HEA magnetocaloric properties are not fully understood.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing HEAs with varying oxygen or nitrogen levels against undoped samples.
Magnetization-versus-temperature and heat-capacity-versus-temperature measurements can be used to evaluate the proposed magnetocaloric improvement.
Failure of doped samples to improve relative to undoped samples would falsify the directional hypothesis.
